title: Playlist and Locker
premise: Gideon Okonkwo has survived small-town Ohio by being invisible—until the ghost haunting Hollow Creek High begins leaving notes in his locker, written in ink that vanishes by morning, each one naming him and asking for a song. The ghost turns out to be the imprint of a student who died in 1979, silenced by the same fear Gideon lives with, and it can only rest if someone speaks its unfinished truth aloud. As Gideon investigates with his best friend Dana, whose loyalty is tested when she realizes what he's hiding about himself, he must choose between staying safe and telling the whole town who he is at the championship game. He tells the truth, loses Dana's friendship temporarily, but frees the ghost—and finds that belonging was never something he could earn by hiding.
about_author: Rosalind Amberdale grew up in a rust-belt town smaller than the one she writes about, where the high school gym still smells like 1978. She now teaches music in a city library and swears every building has at least one story stuck inside it, waiting for the right song.

chapters.title: Ink That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A note appears in his locked locker, addressed to him by name, asking 'What song were you afraid to play?' The ink fades before anyone else can see it. Gideon, practiced at invisibility, almost throws it away—but the handwriting matches a name carved inside the locker door: R. Vance, 1979. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking open loneliness.

chapters.title: Duet with a Dead Kid
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with Dana drawn in. Playing the requested song in the empty band room summons fragments—the ghost's memories bleeding into the speakers. Gideon enlists Dana's help without explaining why the ghost chose him. Research reveals Rowan Vance died the night of the 1979 championship, never having told anyone the truth about himself. Emotional beat: the thrill of secret partnership built on Gideon's own secret.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Dana POV. The ghost's presence grows desperate as the championship approaches—the anniversary of its death. Dana discovers Gideon's notes to himself and confronts him; feeling deceived, she walks away. The ghost shows Gideon its final night: it died running from exposure, and only a public truth spoken in the same place can free it. Emotional beat: betrayal, then understanding that silence protects no one.

chapters.title: Everything Louder Than Fear
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At halftime of the championship game, Gideon takes the microphone—not just to speak Rowan's name and story, but his own. The gym goes silent, then the ghost's ink blazes across the scoreboard one last time before dissolving into light. Dana finds him afterward; forgiveness is slow but real. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into belonging—he is seen, and still standing.
